source.authors: Savelli I, Novales Flamarique I, Iwanicki T, Taylor JS
source.title: Parallel opsin switches in multiple cone types of the starry flounder retina: tuning visual pigment composition for a demersal life style

method: microspectrophotometry (MSP) of isolated photoreceptors, absorbance maximum of the visual pigment
conditions: large post-metamorphic juvenile (mean 196.2 g, n = 3 fish); MSP temperature, adaptation state and fixation not stated in the sentences read; Fig. 1
where: Results, Visual pigments and chromophores in the retina of large juvenile starry flounder
quote: These consisted of two S visual pigments with λmax at 445 nm (n = 19) and 459 nm (n = 17), …
note: Licence: Crossref lists CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0); text read from the PMC copy (PMC5859124). Species printed and filed as Platichthys stellatus (starry flounder), Pleuronectidae, Pleuronectiformes; FishBase (species 4249) and the GBIF species page carry it as a main entry, but neither page stated an explicit accepted status and WoRMS could not be reached, so accepted status is unconfirmed by a status line. Large post-metamorphic juveniles (mean 196.2 g, 22.6 cm, three fish); the same paper reports small juveniles (5.4 g) with a rod at 507 nm and UV (369) and S (415) pigments absent in the large fish, so the value belongs to this size class only. Preparation: isolated photoreceptors; the Methods sentences read give no MSP temperature, fixation or dark-adaptation state (dark adaptation for 3 hours is stated only for the HPLC part); fish held at 10 to 15 C and killed between 13:00 and 14:00. Per-class n is the number of photoreceptors, pooled from three fish. n = 17 photoreceptors. The sentence also gives an S pigment at 445 nm (n = 19); the Results say the S (445) pigment consisted of two pigments (co-expression of two opsins), so 445 is not logged here as a single pigment.

source.authors: Stieb SM, de Busserolles F, Carleton KL, Cortesi F, Chung W-S, Dalton BE, Hammond LA, Marshall NJ
source.title: A detailed investigation of the visual system and visual ecology of the Barrier Reef anemonefish, Amphiprion akindynos

method: microspectrophotometry (MSP) of photoreceptors (mean ± SD, n photoreceptors); compared in the paper with estimates from opsin sequences
conditions: 3 fish kept in aquaria for 4 to 6 months; MSP temperature, adaptation state and preparation in the Supplementary Information (not read)
where: Results, visual pigments (MSP against opsin-based estimates)
quote: In theory, λmax values should match between approaches. This was the case for the rods, where MSP and estimates revealed a λmax of 498 ± 4 nm (n = 23) and 496 nm, respectively.
note: Licence: Crossref lists CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0); text read from the Springer article page. Amphiprion akindynos is ACCEPTED in the repository's GBIF match list (usageKey 5212068). MSP on three fish kept in aquaria for 4 months (one fish) or 6 months (two fish); the main-text Methods say only that MSP followed a standard protocol (Hart 2004), with details in the Supplementary Information, which was not read, so temperature, fixation and adaptation state are not recorded here. The paper compares MSP with values estimated from opsin gene sequences. 498 ± 4 nm, n = 23 photoreceptors; the opsin-based estimate for RH1 was 496 nm.

source.authors: Garm A, Bielecki J, Petie R, Nilsson D-E
source.title: Hunting in Bioluminescent Light: Vision in the Nocturnal Box Jellyfish Copula sivickisi

eye: upper and lower lens eyes of the rhopalia (both fitted to the same single opsin)
method: extracellular ERG spectral sensitivity fitted with a vertebrate-type opsin absorption template (least squares); peak of the fitted template, not a measured pigment
conditions: equal-quanta series 410 to 680 nm; 15 min dark adaptation; 29 C seawater; 7 upper and 7 lower lens eyes from 11 adults
where: Results, Spectral sensitivity; Methods, Electrophysiology; Figure 5
quote: Using the least square of the mean method to fit the spectral sensitivity curve of the lens eyes … returned the best match in both lens eyes to a single opsin peaking at 458 nm (Figure 5).
note: Licence: Crossref/Frontiers state CC BY 4.0 (the article says it is distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution License). Copula sivickisi is ACCEPTED in the repository's GBIF match list (usageKey 5842331); family Tripedaliidae, order Carybdeida as on main. Electroretinogram (ERG, extracellular) spectral sensitivity, not a pigment measurement: equal-quanta (6 × 10^18 photons/s/sr/m2) spectral series over 410 to 680 nm in 20 steps after 15 min dark adaptation, 25 ms flashes, rhopalia in seawater at 29 C (salinity 33 psu), seven lower lens eyes and seven upper lens eyes from 11 adult animals of both sexes; the 458 nm is the opsin-template fit (Govardovskii et al. 2000 templates) to those curves, and the tested range ends at 410 and 680 nm. The sentence before it says both curves had a single peak in the deep blue around 460 nm (Figure 5); the abstract says about 460 nm. Only the two lens-eye types were recorded; pit and slit eyes were not.
